Use exactly that list in every step, and never let a target or excluded column reach a fitted transformer or model.

Never feed derived or renamed columns back into a raw-column frontend.

[RL-0014] When repairing, read the error type and message in the diagnostics first and change the smallest part of the script that causes it; keep the approach, inputs and outputs. A message about specifying columns with strings on non-dataframes means an array reached a name-based transformer (see RL-0009 and RL-0011). A KeyError on a JSON key means a guessed structure; use the keys the file has. Messages starting with 'MLCA:' state an engine rule; comply, do not work around it.
[RL-0015] When the training table has more than 100000 rows, avoid methods whose cost grows with the square of the row count (full silhouette, kernel SVMs, pairwise distances, t-SNE, agglomerative clustering) and prefer linear models with saga or SGD solvers, HistGradientBoosting or MiniBatchKMeans. [RL-0018] Several categorical targets need MultiOutputClassifier or an estimator supporting multiple outputs, with the target DataFrame in _protocol['targets'] order. predict_proba returns one array per target. Do not pass the whole multiclass-multioutput categorical matrix to f1_score, accuracy_score or hamming_loss; these do not support this target form. Compute each score on each target separately and average the per-target values; compute subset accuracy directly as the mean of rows whose target predictions all match. Compute f1_score(average='macro') separately on each target's one-dimensional true and predicted labels, then report the unweighted mean and per-target values. Both vectors must have the same native label type; an object array of encoded integers can be rejected as unknown. Preserve categorical labels directly; target columns are never inputs to fit_record, which refuses them, so do not fit target encoders. Never fit anything during validation or test.
[RL-0026] Persist the full row-preserving feature transformation contract, not just an estimator fitted after transient DataFrame mutations. Parsing, derived features, column selection and ordering needed later must be reproducible by the saved importable pipeline. Learned transforms fit only on the frozen training rows. Deterministic table preparation may precede the split only through a declared prepared-data artifact. Later steps pass the declared source feature schema to the saved pipeline, never assume derived columns already exist in a freshly loaded partition. Inspect fitted input names; do not invent missing columns or fit replacement preprocessing during evaluation.

Chain an object after another only when its feature_names_in_ match the other's output names.
Read the declared _protocol JSON: use _protocol['task']['primary_metric'], _protocol['targets'], _protocol['excluded_columns'] and the declared outcome columns. primary_metric is nested inside task, not a top-level key.
